q: Which is the most accurate description of chemiosmosis in mitochondria?
options: H+ flow back into the matrix through ATP synthase, rotating part of it so it phosphorylates ADP
H+ are actively pumped through ATP synthase into the intermembrane space, using up ATP as they go
Electrons pass through ATP synthase, and their energy is used to bond Pi directly to ADP
Water moves by osmosis through ATP synthase, and the force of the flowing water generates the ATP
explanation: Chemiosmosis (Peter Mitchell's theory) = ATP synthesis coupled to protons diffusing down their electrochemical gradient through ATP synthase. Proton flow turns the enzyme's rotor; the resulting shape changes in its catalytic head bind ADP + Pi and release ATP. It is called oxidative phosphorylation because the gradient comes from oxidation reactions feeding the ETC. 'Osmosis' here means movement across a membrane, not water.
